literal: Inside having hidden, by the local town they will be laughed at, always, liquor having hidden eyes those who droop.
translation: Those who secretly drink liquor and let their intoxicated eyes droop will always be laughed at by the whole town, even if they think they are hiding it inside.
modern: கள்ளை மறைத்துக் குடித்துவிட்டுப் போதையால் கண்கள் சொருகுபவர்கள், தாங்கள் குடித்ததை மனத்திற்குள் மறைத்தாலும், உள்ளூர் மக்களால் எக்காலத்தும் சிரிக்கப்படுவார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet mocks the foolishness of secret drinkers. The word 'ஒற்றி' (from 'ஒற்றுதல்') is used here in the sense of hiding or concealing. A person might consume liquor in secret and try to hide the fact in their mind ('உள் ஒற்றி'). However, the physical effects of intoxication, such as drooping eyes, cannot be concealed. Consequently, their secret is exposed, and they become a constant laughingstock to the people of their town.
